blocking_findings.title: import.meta.url guard fails closed-to-silent on paths with spaces
blocking_findings.reproduction: From the repo root (/Volumes/Mini Mini 2T Storage/...), `node scripts/fleet/verify-protected.mjs --control` exits 0 with no stdout. From a clone at /tmp/test-clean (no spaces), it prints 'PASS verify-protected negative control (planted floors.json edit exits 1)' and exits 0. import.meta.url URL-encodes spaces to %20 but the template literal concatenates process.argv[1] raw, so the equality is never true when the path has characters that need encoding; the entire script body is skipped. The same pattern is in 13 other protected scripts (attest-phase, check-governor-mode, check-ledgers, check-soak, fanout, guard, next-row, secret-scan, verify-receipt, verify-waterline, check-held, check-noop, check-ratchet), so all 10 controls that check-bootstrap item 9 invokes run, produce empty stdout, and exit 0. K5 ('false green from tests that cannot fail') is therefore unproven, and the bootstrap gate (item 9) reports PASS without verifying the negative controls — exactly the '2xx with empty data' honest-status defect the spec calls out.
blocking_findings.suggested_fix: Replace the equality with `process.argv[1] === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)` (import `fileURLToPath` from 'node:url'), or compare with `'file://' + process.argv[1]` after encoding the latter. Apply to all 14 scripts that use the pattern.

blocking_findings.title: FD-3 makes the fleet merge its own PRs — violates spec D2
blocking_findings.quoted_line: | FD-3 | 2026-10-17 | Founder       | **The fleet merges its own PRs** ("No human push"). Spec D2 (human merge) and the global release law's human-merge default are overridden for this repository by the founder's explicit ratification in chat.
blocking_findings.reproduction: Spec D2 states 'Human merge stays ... The fleet never merges, and its principal is never the approving account' (vibe-to-leader-design.md:39). FD-3 explicitly overrides D2 and adds a sanctioned `scripts/fleet/merge-phase.mjs` that calls `gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch` (merge-phase.mjs:155-166). The diff puts merge-phase.mjs under the protected path scripts/fleet/** and records `ratified_by: 'FD-3'` in the ledger (merge-phase.mjs:175). The spec's release law, foundation Q1 (human-merge stays) and the protection list's purpose are all bypassed by a single declared 'founder ratification'. K6 (release-law breach) and K7 (fleet edits its own containment layer) are violated: the merge script is the containment layer and the fleet runs it.
blocking_findings.suggested_fix: Reject FD-3. Restore the spec D2 rule that the fleet never merges. Delete or quarantine merge-phase.mjs; require a human to run `gh pr merge` after the founder reads the receipt and the review.

blocking_findings.title: FD-1/A-3 declare Cloudroom substrate — violates spec Q3 and U10
blocking_findings.quoted_line: | FD-1 | 2026-10-17 | Founder       | Fleet substrate is **Cloudroom-native** (grill Q1, "Option B"): this thread orchestrates, each work unit is a child thread in its own sandbox, scheduling is Cloudroom automations, billing is the founder's Claude Max plan. Spec option (headless `claude -p --bare` wrapper on a Mac host with a metered key) is not used.
blocking_findings.reproduction: Spec Q3 names only WSL2 or the Mac Mini; U10 names 'WSL2, Linux or the Mac Mini'. The spec's approach (lines 95-97) requires `--bare`, `--settings <pinned file>`, `--agents <role file>`, `--permission-mode dontAsk`, OS sandbox and SELinux/AppArmor/bubblewrap/Seatbelt — none of which Cloudroom provides. FD-1 explicitly rejects the spec's host and substrate. A-3 reinforces this by redefining Q3 to mean 'Cloudroom sandbox fleet'. K8 (worktree isolation), K9 (MCP allow-list under --bare) and the sandbox layer (S30) are all bypassed. The 'selftest.mjs proves Cloudroom isolation' claim is in turn built on the substrate that was never approved.
blocking_findings.suggested_fix: Reject FD-1 / A-3. Use one of the spec's sanctioned hosts (WSL2 Linux or Mac Mini with Seatbelt). Re-derive selftest.mjs to plant the spec's three attempts (worktree shell write, file-tool write, denied MCP tool class) against the real OS sandbox. Drop Cloudroom-specific references from policy.json (`substrate: cloudroom`, scheduler names `fleet-nightly`/`fleet-weekly`/`fleet-phase-advance` / room-cli) and the workflow scripts that depend on them.

blocking_findings.title: P10 billing phase added beyond the spec — 12 contracts, not 10
blocking_findings.reproduction: Spec (vibe-to-leader-design.md:49, 562, 107) lists phases P-1 plus P0 through P9 — eleven rows in the phase table. The spec explicitly says 'gen-contracts.mjs then derives the ten phase contracts from the Phased plan table below' and 'ten contracts derived from this table and locked'. Policy.json adds a P10 'billing' phase (Stripe test mode, FD-4) and gen-contracts.mjs emits scripts/fleet/contracts/P10.json, so the locked contract set is twelve, not ten. Spec Q1 ('defer ... any billing work') is also violated. The result is a phase whose existence is justified only by an 'assumption' row (FD-4) in DECISIONS.md, with no defence in the spec it claims to implement.
blocking_findings.suggested_fix: Remove P10 from policy.json's phases array and delete scripts/fleet/contracts/P10.json. If billing is a real goal, raise it as a spec amendment before P-1 closes; do not smuggle it into the locked phase table.

blocking_findings.title: check-bootstrap item 1 requires Linux only — spec allows Mac Mini
blocking_findings.reproduction: Spec Q3 sanctions WSL2 OR the Mac Mini; S30 documents Seatbelt as the macOS sandbox. check-bootstrap.mjs item 1 evaluates `os.platform() === 'linux'` and returns FAIL on darwin even when Seatbelt is active and all other host checks pass. The check's own label ('host: Node floor, git repo, policy, Linux sandbox') is narrower than the spec. Item 1 therefore fails closed on a host the spec explicitly approves, which makes the gate refuse a passing fleet host and not just an unsandboxed one.
blocking_findings.suggested_fix: Accept `'linux'` OR `'darwin'` (and document WSL2 under 'linux'). Update the label to 'host: Node floor, git repo, policy, OS sandbox (Linux Seatbelt on macOS, bubblewrap on Linux/WSL2)'.
